question: Can a language model build a high-quality instruction-following dataset by labelling unlabelled web text with instructions and curating it itself, without distillation from stronger models?
hypothesis: Some subset of human-written web text suits as gold responses to instructions, and a model can predict those instructions and select the high-quality pairs.
contributions: Instruction backtranslation: self-augmentation (generate instructions for web text) plus iterative self-curation
Humpback models outperform other non-distilled LLaMa models on the Alpaca leaderboard
Scaling analysis showing quality-filtered augmented data scales better than other instruction datasets

method.summary: A backward model p(x|y) finetuned on 3200 Open Assistant seed pairs generates instructions for 502k ClueWeb segments. A seed-finetuned model M0 rates each pair 1-5 by prompting; pairs with score>=k join seed data to train M1, which rescores to give M2 (two iterations). Seed and augmented data are tagged with different system prompts.
method.task: instruction tuning via self-training on web data

datasets.name: Open Assistant seed
datasets.source: Open Assistant (Köpf et al., 2023), first turn, English, rank 0

datasets.name: ClueWeb English segments
datasets.preprocessing: segments after HTML header; length 600-3000 chars; Jaccard n-gram dedup of sentences; header quality filters (empty, all uppercase, navigation text)

datasets.name: Eval prompt set
datasets.size: 1130 unique prompts from Vicuna 80, Self-instruct 252, Open Assistant 188, Koala 156, HH_RLHF 129, LIMA 300, authors 64
datasets.split: 256 prompts (excluding AlpacaEval test) as dev set

models.name: Backward model Myx
models.init_from: LLaMA finetuned on (output, instruction) seed pairs

other.use: AlpacaEval judge; also compared as data selector in Table 9

training.objective: supervised finetuning, loss on output tokens only
training.lr_schedule: linear decay to 9e-6 at end of training

other.system_prompt_tags: Sa = 'Answer in the style of an AI Assistant.' seed; Sw = 'Answer with knowledge from web search.' augmented

inference.prompting: inference system prompt {Sa,Sw} concatenated gave best win rate (Table 5)

parameters.curation_threshold_k: k=4 or 5 reported (A4: score>=4, A5: score>=4.5 per Sec 3.3)

metrics.name: AlpacaEval win rate
metrics.definition: pairwise win rate vs text-davinci-003 judged by GPT-4

metrics.name: human pairwise preference
metrics.definition: MTurk workers choose better/worse/tie, order randomized

metrics.name: zero-shot accuracy
metrics.definition: perplexity of correct answer on SIQA, PIQA, Arc-E, Arc-C, OBQA, MMLU

metrics.name: scaling coefficient alpha
metrics.definition: fit w = alpha log N + C of win rate on N examples

eval.protocol: GPT-4 judge via AlpacaEval; human eval with 29 MTurk workers screened from 1000 applicants (agreement >85% on 10 screening examples); single run, standard errors on some tables; no seeds stated

prompts.text: Below is an instruction from an user and a candidate answer. Evaluate whether or not the answer is a good example of how AI Assistant should respond to the user's instruction. Please assign a score using the following 5-point scale: 1-5 (rubric in Table 19: 1 incomplete/off-topic/forum-like; 2 addresses most asks but not directly; 3 helpful but not AI-assistant style; 4 AI-assistant perspective, minor room for improvement; 5 perfect answer). Please first provide a brief reasoning you used to derive the rating score, and then write "Score: <rating>" in the last line.

results.claim: Training on augmented data without self-curation does not improve instruction following despite more data; high-quality self-curated subsets keep improving with scale (values only in Fig 2).
results.setup: 7B LLaMa, data sizes 3200 to 25600, win rate vs text-davinci-003
results.quote: We find that training on augmented data without self-curation does not improve instruction following performance despite scaling up data quantity.

results.claim: Authors contrast their finding with the superficial alignment hypothesis: more high-quality data gives further gains.
results.quote: Our results provide a contrasting observation that increasing the quantity of high-quality data provides further gains (whereas increased quantities of low-quality data does not).

results.claim: System-prompt tagging helps: train with Sa/Sw tags and infer with combined {Sa,Sw} gives 66.47% vs 59.96% with no system prompt in training or inference.

results.claim: Instruction backtranslation: seed model predicts instructions for web text, then curates pairs by 1-5 self-rating, keeping score>=k.
results.quote: The seed model is used to construct training examples by generating instruction prompts for web documents (self-augmentation), and then selecting high quality examples from among these candidates (self-curation).

limits: Web-sourced augmented data may amplify biases; CrowS-Pairs measures bias detection, not generation (App A.1)
Safety not optimised; tested only on 30 sensitive prompts (App A.2)

Self-curation precision is low (0.44-0.52) for M0/M1 (Table 9)
Optimizer, hardware, compute, seeds and code/data availability not stated
Larger corpora not tried; Humpback 70B still below LLaMa2 Chat
Mostly GPT-4-judged win rates; LLM judge
